program_overview.title: Mathematics for Data Science and Analytics
program_overview.tagline: The difference between running models and understanding them is mathematics. This is that mathematics, taught honestly in twelve months.
program_overview.description:
Every data career eventually hits the same wall: the tools are easy, the mathematics behind them is not, and interviews, promotions and real analytical judgment all live on the far side of that wall. This live online course teaches exactly the mathematics data work stands on: statistics that tell the truth, probability that calibrates uncertainty, the linear algebra inside every model, regression and classification understood from first principles, optimization, the mathematics of neural networks, Bayesian methods, time series, and the experimental design behind honest A/B testing.

The course is deliberately practical about rigor: every concept is derived enough to be owned, then immediately exercised on real data questions, the kind analysts and data scientists actually face. Statistical malpractice gets named and corrected throughout: p-hacking, leakage, confounding, the graph that lies. By the end, a student does not just know the formulas; they know which analysis is honest and can defend it in an interview or a meeting.

The pace is real: two live classes a week plus four to six hours of practice fits the syllabus in twelve months, and learners who need longer take up to fourteen, the batch adapts. Assessment is honest too: problem sets after every class, monthly mixed reviews that reach back deliberately, phase exams, and a final exam that decides the certificate, with focused revision and a free retest for those who fall short. Real knowledge, real work, depth over dopamine.

faqs.question: What exactly does this maths for data science course teach?
faqs.answer: The mathematics data careers actually stand on, in four phases: statistics and probability that tell the truth; linear algebra through eigenvalues and PCA plus honest statistical inference; the mathematics of machine learning, regression, classification, trees, clustering and evaluation from first principles; and modern practice, optimization, neural network mathematics, Bayesian methods, time series and A/B testing, ending in a capstone analysis on real data.

faqs.question: How long does it take to learn the maths for data science?
faqs.answer: Honestly: 12 months at 2 live classes a week plus 4 to 6 hours of practice, and the course keeps 2 months of margin in hand for learners who need more repetition, up to 14 months with no penalty. Crash courses compress this into weeks by skipping the understanding; the wall they skip is exactly what interviews and real work then test.

faqs.question: How is progress measured? Is the certificate just for attending?
faqs.answer: No. Problem sets follow every class and come back with written feedback, monthly reviews deliberately mix new material with earlier topics so nothing fades, each phase ends with an exam, and the course ends with a final exam, written plus practical, that decides the certificate. Falling short earns a focused revision plan and a free retest. The certificate certifies knowledge, not attendance.

faqs.question: Do I need to know programming or calculus already?
faqs.answer: Neither. School mathematics is the entry bar; the calculus that appears is refreshed as needed, and code is used only as a calculator, spreadsheets and light Python, because the mathematics is the syllabus. Students who already code simply see the connections faster.

faqs.question: How is this different from a data science bootcamp?
faqs.answer: Bootcamps teach tools and hope the mathematics arrives by osmosis; it does not. This course is the missing layer: the statistics, linear algebra and ML mathematics that make tool skills defensible in interviews and reliable at work. The two pair well, our Data Analysis course covers the tooling side, and this course makes it mean something.

faqs.question: Will this help me in analytics interviews and real work?
faqs.answer: Directly: probability puzzles, hypothesis testing, regression interpretation, evaluation metrics and A/B test design are the exact backbone of analytics and data science interviews, and the course drills them with written defense, not just computation. At work, the payoff is judgment: knowing which analysis is honest, and being the person in the room who can say why.

faqs.question: Does this cover deep learning and AI?
faqs.answer: It covers their mathematics honestly: optimization, gradient descent and the mathematics of neural networks, computed by hand on small networks, plus a clear map of where transformers and attention sit. Full deep learning practice, building and training real models, is our AI and Machine Learning Masterclass, which assumes exactly the mathematics this course builds.

faqs.question: Can I take a trial class?
faqs.answer: Yes, a free demo class with no commitment: book at learn.modernagecoders.com/contact or message us on WhatsApp at +91 91233 66161. Bring a statistics question from your own work or study; the demo is best when it runs on your real problem.

faqs.question: Are lessons live or self-paced videos?
faqs.answer: Live, always: small groups where problems are worked together and your reasoning gets corrected in real time, never pre-recorded videos. Mathematical judgment is built under feedback; a video cannot tell you why your hypothesis test is invalid.
